newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to meet advisers on Mexico decision.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to meet advisers on Mexico decision.

text.p: President Bill Clinton planned to meet Secretary of State Madeleine Albright and other top advisers on Friday to hear her recommendation on whether to certify Mexico as a U.S. ally in the drug war.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters he would not rule out Clinton making a final decision on the hotly debated Mexico issue on Friday but it could require more work and conceivably could lapse until Monday.
Another official, however, said there was "still a good possibility" of a decision on Friday afternoon. Albright was expected at the White House at midday.

Clinton must decide whether he will approve or disqualify Mexico and 31 other countries in an annual evaluation known as the "certification" process. If a country is decertified economic sanctions are possible.

Mexico, the United States' third biggest trade partner, has always passed that test since it was instituted by law in 1986, despite U.S. concerns about government corruption. But the firing last week of Mexico's anti-narcotics chief for allegedly taking bribes from a drug kingpin has put the U.S. decision in doubt.
There was speculation that Clinton would decertify Mexico but waive sanctions for now to give Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo time to show he is working on the problem.
